about: Every model the swarm can be made of, be decided by, or be brought to parity with, and the engine that runs them. Each file is pinned: a repository, a revision, a size and a SHA-256, as Hugging Face (and, for the engine, GitHub) listed them on 2026-11-15. Only LFM2.5 2.6B, Bonsai 2 2B, Kev 4B, StartLux Decision 4B, Jeffan 4B and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B have been run here; the others are listed as their makers published them and are untried.

atomic.name: Atomic Engine
atomic.about: A developer preview built on llama.cpp. It runs a model within a memory budget and, for Inkling 2 Mini, lets a small draft model propose tokens the model checks. Built from source at a pinned commit: it needs the Xcode command line tools; CMake is fetched for it.

enginesAbout: engine: what serves a model here. "llama": a GGUF file served by llama.cpp. "tensorfold": an MLX build, a folder of files (dir; file is its weights and parts the files beside it), served by TensorFold on an Apple silicon Mac. A model both engines serve has an entry for each: another quantisation is another member, with its own record. Tried here with TensorFold 1.3.1, 2026-11-20: it serves LFM3 1.7B and Qwen3.5 2B, and refuses LFM2.5 1.2B and 2.6B (no backend for lfm2 checkpoints).

deciders.about: No decision model is loaded. Where the drafts differ, one slot of the swarm is shown every different answer and its word settles it (SwOA specification O.6.6, HOW alone). A judge must be named for training, since no decider is there to read whether two answers say the same.

targets.name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B
targets.needs: an Apple silicon Mac with TensorFold

serve.why: Served without drafts: with them this model's replies break off into a token that is no real choice (the last of its vocabulary, shown as <unk>), part-way through code it is copying. Learned in The Crew on this model, and seen again here.

decidersAbout: The models that can decide. Every one answers the same request (POST /v1/systemone: a state and typed questions, a probability for each option), so any of them can stand in the decide step. index: its balanced score on the community Decision Index (multimodalart/jev-decision-index, Decision Index 0.4.1, read 2026-11-16, 300 models; Jev 1.14, TypeSafe's hosted model, scores 60.24; the deciders listed are its leaders at each size with weights on Hugging Face, pinned at the revision named), and the entry it was scored as. runsOn: 'mac' (Apple silicon) and 'cuda' (an NVIDIA GPU), as its maker documents it. serve: how training/kev.sh fetches and starts it here ('kev'; 'startlux-mlx', through MLX; 'llama', one GGUF file its maker made for stock llama.cpp, whose llama-server answers /v1/systemone itself, served with the maker's flags); 'cuda' ones are listed with their maker's own instructions and are not started by the swarm.
